title: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 Reads DNA One Cell Type at a Time
dek: The new model predicts how DNA variants act inside specific human cells.
caption:
The same DNA typo can be harmless in one cell and trouble in another. Google DeepMind just built an AI to tell the difference. 🧬

AlphaGenome 2 predicts how small DNA changes play out inside specific human cell types, like a heart muscle cell or a gut immune cell. The original AlphaGenome looked at broad tissue averages. The new model reads 1 million DNA letters at once, trains on 107M+ single-cell profiles across 68 tissues, and adds DNA methylation predictions.

On the TenK10K immune cell benchmark it found 30% of causal variants vs 16% before. It even picked out the ETS2 variant tied to inflammatory bowel disease in gut macrophages. The catch: it costs more to run, so the first model still powers the genome-wide AlphaGenome Atlas.

Why it matters: drugs target specific proteins in specific cells, so knowing where a variant acts could speed up drug discovery. It's free for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API and not for clinical use. We're following this one closely at AI Parabellum.

post_caption:
From tissue averages to single cells: AlphaGenome 2 is DeepMind's sharpest look yet at how genetic variants affect disease.

It nearly doubles the variants it finds that change gene expression, handles new cell states without retraining, and is available now to non-commercial researchers through the AlphaGenome API. 🔬
